prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://nodejs.org/en/about/releases/ | QUOTE: "Initial active development of the major release happens on the main branch. Once the major version is ready for release, it will be branched and become an LTS release line. After the LTS release line is cut, the release will be in Current for 6 months. After that, it will transition to Active LTS for 12 months." | CLAIM: This shows that a Node.js LTS release has a 12-month Active LTS period.  
SOURCE: https://nodejs.org/en/about/releases/ | QUOTE: "After Active LTS, a release moves to Maintenance LTS for 18 months, where only critical bug fixes, security updates, and documentation updates will be backported. After the Maintenance LTS phase, the release will reach End-of-Life (EOL) and will no longer be supported." | CLAIM: This shows that a Node.js LTS release has an 18-month Maintenance LTS period before it reaches End-of-Life.
